decisions.choice: spoke ... saying: the opening of a new speech
decisions.reason: The usual opening of a speech of God to Moses, as in 1:1. This speech, on the holy food of the priests, runs to verse 16.

decisions.reason: The three speech openings of this chapter (verses 1, 17, 26) follow the French style guide; the laws themselves use the future at Literal and Balanced and "doit" or the imperative at Readable.

records.literal_gloss: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, and they will separate themselves from [the] holy things of [the] sons of Israel, and not they will profane [the] name of my holiness, which they [are] consecrating to me; I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they keep themselves apart from the holy things of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and [that] they not profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, [the things] which they consecrate to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: "Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy gifts that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set apart for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and so not profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: "Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy gifts that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set apart for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Then they will not dishonor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: «Habla a Aarón y a sus hijos, para que se mantengan apartados de las cosas santas de los hijos de Israel, y [para que] no profanen {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} santo nombre, [las cosas] que ellos {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} consagran. Yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: «Di a Aarón y a sus hijos que tengan cuidado con las ofrendas santas que los israelitas apartan para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y que así no profanen {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} santo nombre. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: «Diles a Aarón y a sus hijos que traten con cuidado las ofrendas santas que los israelitas separan para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Así no deshonrarán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} santo nombre. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: « Parle à Aaron et à ses fils, pour qu’ils se tiennent à l’écart des choses saintes des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, et [qu’ils] ne profanent pas {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} saint nom, [les choses] qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} consacrent. Je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: « Dis à Aaron et à ses fils de prendre garde aux dons saints que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} consacrent, afin de ne pas profaner {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} saint nom. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: « Dis à Aaron et à ses fils de faire attention aux dons saints que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} mettent à part pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Ainsi, ils ne déshonoreront pas {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} saint nom. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: "Sema na Haruni na wanawe, ili wajitenge na vitu vitakatifu vya wana wa Israeli, na [ili] wasilitie unajisi jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} takatifu, [vitu] wanavyoniwekea wakfu. Mimi [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: "Waambie Haruni na wanawe wawe waangalifu na matoleo matakatifu ambayo Waisraeli wananitengea, ili wasilitie unajisi jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} takatifu. Mimi ndimi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: "Waambie Haruni na wanawe wayashughulikie kwa uangalifu matoleo matakatifu ambayo Waisraeli wananitengea. Hivyo hawatalivunjia heshima jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} takatifu. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: the holy things: the gifts Israel sets apart for God, including the food the priests eat
decisions.reason: The word covers everything the people consecrate to God: the priests' portions of the sacrifices (6:9-11; 7:31-34; 10:12-15), the firstfruits, the tithes and things given by vow (Numbers 18:8-19). They belong to God, and the priests and their households eat them as his gift. This chapter is mostly about that holy food. The clause "which they consecrate to me" comes after "my holy name" in Hebrew, but it describes the holy things: it is the Israelites who set them apart for God, as verse 3 says.

decisions.choice: keep themselves apart from: hold back from the holy things whenever they may not touch them
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for a Nazirite, one set apart (Numbers 6:2). It means to separate oneself from something, to hold back from it, and so to treat it with reverence. Verses 3-9 show what is meant: a priest who is unclean must not come near the holy things or eat them until he is clean.

decisions.choice: profane my holy name: treat what belongs to God as common, and so dishonor God himself
decisions.reason: To profane is to make common, to take what is holy into ordinary use (19:12; 21:6). God's name stands for God himself as he has made himself known (Exodus 3:15; 20:7). When a priest handles the holy gifts carelessly, the dishonor falls on the God to whom they belong. "My holy name" is literally "the name of my holiness" (20:3; Ezekiel 36:20-23). The same warning closes the chapter (verse 32).

decisions.choice: be careful with the holy gifts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the separation means in practice, following m2: the priests must take care with the holy gifts and not touch them when unclean. Literal keeps "keep themselves apart from the holy things".

decisions.choice: dishonor
decisions.reason: Readable says "dishonor" for "profane", the common word for what profaning God's name does. Literal and Balanced keep "profane".

decisions.choice: [the things] which they consecrate to me
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the clause in its Hebrew place and supplies "the things" so that it is not read as describing the name. Balanced and Readable move it next to "the holy gifts", which it describes.

decisions.choice: "las cosas santas" (L); "las ofrendas santas" (B, R), and "la comida santa" where the English says "holy food"
decisions.reason: The same three forms are kept through verses 2-16 for the priests' holy portions, as the English moves between "holy things", "holy gifts" and "holy food".

decisions.choice: "les choses saintes" (L); "les dons saints" (B, R), and "la nourriture sainte" where the English says "holy food"
decisions.reason: The same three forms are kept through verses 2-16 for the priests' holy portions, as the English moves between "holy things", "holy gifts" and "holy food".

decisions.choice: "kulitia unajisi" (L, B); "kulivunjia heshima" (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no single verb for "profane". "Kutia unajisi", to make common or unclean, is used for profaning holy things and God's name, as in Exodus 31; Readable says "kuvunjia heshima", to dishonor, as the English Readable does. Holy things are "vitu vitakatifu" (L) and "matoleo matakatifu" or "chakula kitakatifu" (B, R) through verse 16.

source.text: אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם לְדֹרֹ֨תֵיכֶ֜ם כָּל־אִ֣ישׁ׀אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרַ֣ב מִכָּל־זַרְעֲכֶ֗ם אֶל־הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְדִּ֤ישׁוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְטֻמְאָת֖וֹ עָלָ֑יו וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֧פֶשׁ הַהִ֛וא מִלְּפָנַ֖י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Say to them, for your generations, every man who draws near from all your offspring to the holy things which consecrate [the] sons of Israel to Yahweh, and his uncleanness [is] on him, and will be cut off the person that from before me; I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: Say to them, 'For your generations, any man of all your offspring who comes near to the holy things that the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel consecrate to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while his uncleanness [is] on him, that person shall be cut off from before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'
en.B: Say to them: 'For all your generations, if any man among your descendants comes near the holy gifts that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} consecrate to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while he is unclean, that person must be cut off from before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'
en.R: Tell them, 'For all time to come, none of your descendants may come near the holy gifts while he is unclean. These are the gifts the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set apart as holy for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Anyone who does so must be removed from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'

Yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}”.
es.B: Diles: “En todas {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} generaciones, si algún hombre de entre {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} descendientes se acerca a las ofrendas santas que los israelitas consagran {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} estando impuro, esa persona será cortada de delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}”.
es.R: Diles: “Desde ahora y para siempre, ninguno de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} descendientes debe acercarse a las ofrendas santas mientras esté impuro. Son las ofrendas que los israelitas apartan como santas para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Quien lo haga tiene que ser expulsado de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} presencia. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}”.

sw.L: Waambie, 'Katika vizazi vyenu, kila mtu wa uzao wenu wote atakayekaribia vitu vitakatifu ambavyo wana wa Israeli humwekea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wakfu, hali unajisi wake [u] juu yake, mtu huyo atakatiliwa mbali kutoka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Mimi [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.'
sw.B: Waambie, 'Katika vizazi vyenu vyote, mtu yeyote wa uzao wenu akikaribia matoleo matakatifu ambayo Waisraeli humwekea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wakfu, naye yu najisi, mtu huyo atakatiliwa mbali kutoka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Mimi ndimi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.'
sw.R: Waambie, 'Tangu sasa na hata milele, yeyote wa wazao wenu asikaribie matoleo matakatifu akiwa najisi. Hayo ndiyo matoleo ambayo Waisraeli humtengea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kuwa matakatifu. Yeyote atakayefanya hivyo lazima aondolewe mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.'

decisions.choice: comes near ... while his uncleanness is on him: handles or eats the holy things while unclean
decisions.reason: To come near the holy things is to touch them or eat them (verses 4-7). The man meant is any descendant of Aaron, a priest by birth. The danger is not the holy food itself but a priest bringing his uncleanness into contact with what is holy (7:20-21; 15:31).

decisions.choice: cut off from before me: removed from God's presence
decisions.reason: This is the penalty of being cut off (7:20), here put as "from before me": the priest who serves in God's presence loses his place before him. It is God who acts, as in 20:3-6.

decisions.choice: three short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long Hebrew sentence into the rule, the description of the holy gifts and the penalty.

source.text: אִ֣ישׁ אִ֞ישׁ מִזֶּ֣רַע אַהֲרֹ֗ן וְה֤וּא צָר֨וּעַ֙ א֣וֹ זָ֔ב בַּקֳּדָשִׁים֙ לֹ֣א יֹאכַ֔ל עַ֖ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְהָ֑ר וְהַנֹּגֵ֨עַ֙ בְּכָל־טְמֵא־נֶ֔פֶשׁ א֣וֹ אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־תֵּצֵ֥א מִמֶּ֖נּוּ שִׁכְבַת־זָֽרַע׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] man, [a] man of [the] offspring of Aaron, and he [has a] scale disease or [a] discharge, in the holy things not he will eat until that he is clean; and the [one] who touches any unclean [by a] person, or [a] man who goes out from him [an] emission of seed,

en.L: Any man of the offspring of Aaron who has scale disease or a discharge shall not eat of the holy things until he is clean. And whoever touches anything unclean through a dead person, or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out,
en.B: No man descended from Aaron who has a serious skin disease or a discharge may eat any of the holy food until he is clean. Nor may one who touches anything made unclean by a dead body, or a man who has an emission of semen,
en.R: A man from Aaron's family who has a serious skin disease or a discharge from his body must not eat the holy food until he is clean. The same is true if he touches something made unclean by a dead body, or if semen comes out of his body.

es.L: Ningún hombre de la descendencia de Aarón que tenga enfermedad de la piel o flujo comerá de las cosas santas hasta que esté puro. Y el que toque cualquier cosa impura por un muerto, o el hombre del que salga emisión de semen,
es.B: Ningún hombre descendiente de Aarón que tenga una enfermedad grave de la piel o un flujo podrá comer de la comida santa hasta que esté puro. Tampoco podrá el que toque algo que haya quedado impuro por un cadáver, ni el hombre que tenga una emisión de semen,
es.R: Un hombre de la familia de Aarón que tenga una enfermedad grave de la piel o un flujo que le sale del cuerpo no debe comer la comida santa hasta que esté puro. Lo mismo vale si toca algo que quedó impuro por un cadáver, o si le sale semen del cuerpo.

fr.L: Tout homme de la descendance d’Aaron qui a une maladie de peau ou un écoulement ne mangera pas des choses saintes jusqu’à ce qu’il soit pur. Et celui qui touche quoi que ce soit d’impur par un mort, ou un homme dont sort une émission de semence,
fr.B: Aucun homme descendant d’Aaron qui a une maladie de peau grave ou un écoulement ne pourra manger de la nourriture sainte avant d’être pur. Il en va de même pour celui qui touche une chose rendue impure par un cadavre, ou pour l’homme qui a une émission de semence,
fr.R: Un homme de la famille d’Aaron qui a une maladie de peau grave ou un écoulement qui sort de son corps ne doit pas manger la nourriture sainte avant d’être pur. C’est la même chose s’il touche quelque chose qu’un cadavre a rendu impur, ou si de la semence sort de son corps.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote wa uzao wa Haruni aliye na ugonjwa wa ngozi au anayetokwa na majimaji hatakula katika vitu vitakatifu mpaka atakapokuwa safi. Na yeye anayegusa kitu chochote kilicho najisi kwa sababu ya maiti, au mtu ambaye shahawa humtoka,
sw.B: Mwanamume yeyote wa uzao wa Haruni aliye na ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi au anayetokwa na majimaji mwilini asile chakula kitakatifu mpaka awe safi. Vivyo hivyo yeye anayegusa kitu kilichotiwa unajisi na maiti, au mwanamume aliyetokwa na shahawa,
sw.R: Mwanamume wa jamaa ya Haruni aliye na ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi au anayetokwa na majimaji mwilini mwake asile chakula kitakatifu mpaka awe safi. Ndivyo ilivyo pia akigusa kitu kilichotiwa unajisi na maiti, au akitokwa na shahawa.

decisions.choice: scale disease or a discharge: the long-lasting kinds of uncleanness
decisions.reason: Scale disease (13:2) and a discharge from the body (15:2) last until they heal, and the man is then cleansed with offerings (14:1-32; 15:13-15). Until then the priest may not eat the holy food. The other cases in verses 4-6 last only until evening.

decisions.choice: unclean through a dead person: made unclean by contact with a corpse
decisions.reason: The word for person here means a dead person, as in 21:1, 11 and Numbers 19:11-13. Whatever has touched a corpse passes the uncleanness on.

decisions.choice: or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out: the priest himself, as in 15:16
alternatives: or who touches a man who has an emission of semen
decisions.reason: The clause most likely describes the priest himself, in a series of cases each opened by "or a man" (verse 5). It may instead continue "whoever touches": one who touches a man who has had an emission. Either way the uncleanness lasts until evening (15:16-17).

decisions.choice: any man / no man
decisions.reason: The doubled word means "any man" (17:3). These laws are for the priests, so no gender setting is used. Balanced puts the ruling first as "No man ... may eat" and carries it into the cases that follow.

decisions.choice: The same is true if ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs on to the end of verse 6. Readable gives each case in a sentence of its own.

source.text: אוֹ־אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִגַּ֔ע בְּכָל־שֶׁ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְמָא־ל֑וֹ א֤וֹ בְאָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְמָא־ל֔וֹ לְכֹ֖ל טֻמְאָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: or [a] man who touches any swarming thing which makes him unclean, or [a] human who makes him unclean, with all his uncleanness,

en.L: or a man who touches any swarming thing by which he becomes unclean, or a human being by whom he becomes unclean, whatever his uncleanness,
en.B: or one who touches any swarming creature that makes him unclean, or a human being through whom he becomes unclean in any of the ways a person can be unclean,
en.R: It is also true if he touches any small creature that makes him unclean, or a person who makes him unclean in any way.

es.L: o el hombre que toque cualquier animalillo de los que pululan por el cual quede impuro, o a un ser humano por el cual quede impuro, sea cual sea su impureza,
es.B: o el que toque cualquier animalillo de los que pululan que lo haga impuro, o a un ser humano por medio del cual quede impuro de cualquiera de las maneras en que una persona puede ser impura,
es.R: También vale si toca algún animalito que se arrastra por el suelo y que lo hace impuro, o a una persona que lo hace impuro de cualquier manera.

fr.L: ou l’homme qui touche une petite bête grouillante, quelle qu’elle soit, qui le rend impur, ou un être humain qui le rend impur, quelle que soit son impureté,
fr.B: ou celui qui touche une petite bête grouillante qui le rend impur, ou un être humain qui lui transmet son impureté, de quelque manière qu’une personne puisse être impure,
fr.R: C’est vrai aussi s’il touche une petite bête qui grouille sur le sol et qui le rend impur, ou une personne qui le rend impur d’une façon ou d’une autre.

sw.L: au mtu anayegusa kiumbe chochote kitambaacho ambacho kwacho anakuwa najisi, au binadamu ambaye kwake anakuwa najisi, unajisi wake wowote ule,
sw.B: au anayegusa kiumbe chochote kitambaacho kinachomtia unajisi, au binadamu anayemtia unajisi kwa njia yoyote ambayo mtu anaweza kuwa najisi,
sw.R: Ndivyo ilivyo pia akigusa kiumbe kidogo kitambaacho ardhini kinachomtia unajisi, au mtu anayemtia unajisi kwa njia yoyote.

decisions.choice: swarming thing: small creatures that teem on the ground
decisions.reason: The word covers small creatures such as rats, mice and lizards. Touching their bodies makes a person unclean until evening (11:29-31).

decisions.choice: a human being ... whatever his uncleanness: anyone whose uncleanness passes to the priest
decisions.reason: Some kinds of uncleanness in people pass to those who touch them, such as a discharge (15:7) or a woman's flow (15:19). "Whatever his uncleanness" covers every such kind. The word for human being is the general word, not the word for a man.

source.text: נֶ֚פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּגַּע־בּ֔וֹ וְטָמְאָ֖ה עַד־הָעָ֑רֶב וְלֹ֤א יֹאכַל֙ מִן־הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֛י אִם־רָחַ֥ץ בְּשָׂר֖וֹ בַּמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: [a] person who touches it will be unclean until the evening, and not he will eat from the holy things except if he has washed his flesh in water.

en.L: the person who touches it shall be unclean until the evening, and shall not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.
en.B: the one who has touched it stays unclean until evening and may not eat any of the holy food until he has washed his body in water.
en.R: Any priest who touches such things will be unclean until evening. He must not eat any of the holy food until he has washed his body with water.

es.L: la persona que lo toque será impura hasta la tarde, y no comerá de las cosas santas a menos que haya lavado su cuerpo en agua.
es.B: el que lo haya tocado queda impuro hasta la tarde y no podrá comer nada de la comida santa hasta que haya lavado su cuerpo con agua.
es.R: Cualquier sacerdote que toque esas cosas quedará impuro hasta la tarde. No debe comer nada de la comida santa hasta que se haya lavado el cuerpo con agua.

fr.L: la personne qui touche cela sera impure jusqu’au soir, et ne mangera pas des choses saintes à moins d’avoir lavé son corps dans l’eau.
fr.B: celui qui l’a touché reste impur jusqu’au soir et ne pourra manger aucune nourriture sainte avant d’avoir lavé son corps dans l’eau.
fr.R: Tout prêtre qui touche ces choses sera impur jusqu’au soir. Il ne doit manger aucune nourriture sainte avant de s’être lavé le corps avec de l’eau.

sw.L: mtu atakayekigusa atakuwa najisi mpaka jioni, wala hatakula katika vitu vitakatifu isipokuwa ameuosha mwili wake kwa maji.
sw.B: aliyekigusa atakuwa najisi mpaka jioni, wala asile chochote katika chakula kitakatifu mpaka aoge mwili wake kwa maji.
sw.R: Kuhani yeyote anayegusa vitu hivyo atakuwa najisi mpaka jioni. Asile chakula chochote kitakatifu mpaka aoge mwili wake kwa maji.

decisions.choice: unclean until evening, and washed: two steps to being clean again
decisions.reason: The priest bathes, and his uncleanness ends at sunset (verse 7). Only then may he eat. The same pattern is found in 11:24-25 and 15:5-11. For the holy food, the bath is required, not optional.

decisions.choice: Any priest
decisions.reason: Readable names the person: the cases in verses 4-6 are about Aaron's descendants.

source.text: וּבָ֥א הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וְטָהֵ֑ר וְאַחַר֙ יֹאכַ֣ל מִן־הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֥י לַחְמ֖וֹ הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And goes the sun, and he will be clean, and after he will eat from the holy things, for his food it [is].

en.L: And the sun shall go down, and he will be clean; and afterward he may eat of the holy things, for it [is] his food.
en.B: Once the sun has set he is clean, and then he may eat of the holy food, since that is what he lives on.
en.R: After the sun goes down, he will be clean. Then he may eat the holy food. It is the food the priests live on.

es.L: Y se pondrá el sol, y quedará puro; y después podrá comer de las cosas santas, porque [es] su alimento.
es.B: Cuando se haya puesto el sol, quedará puro, y entonces podrá comer de la comida santa, ya que de ella vive.
es.R: Cuando se ponga el sol, quedará puro. Entonces podrá comer la comida santa. Es la comida de la que viven los sacerdotes.

fr.L: Et le soleil se couchera, et il sera pur ; et ensuite il pourra manger des choses saintes, car c’[est] sa nourriture.
fr.B: Une fois le soleil couché, il est pur, et il peut alors manger de la nourriture sainte, puisque c’est elle qui le fait vivre.
fr.R: Quand le soleil s’est couché, il est pur. Alors il peut manger la nourriture sainte. C’est la nourriture dont les prêtres vivent.

sw.L: Na jua litakapozama, atakuwa safi; na baadaye atakula katika vitu vitakatifu, kwa maana [ni] chakula chake.
sw.B: Jua likishazama, atakuwa safi, kisha anaweza kula chakula kitakatifu, kwa kuwa ndicho anachoishi nacho.
sw.R: Jua likishazama, atakuwa safi. Kisha anaweza kula chakula kitakatifu. Ndicho chakula ambacho makuhani wanaishi kwacho.

decisions.choice: it is his food: the priests live on the holy gifts
decisions.reason: The priests had no land of their own. Their food was their share of the offerings (Numbers 18:8-20; Deuteronomy 18:1-2). So the rule does not take the food away: it only makes him wait until he is clean.

decisions.choice: what he lives on
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "his food" means here, following m1. Literal keeps "his food".

source.text: נְבֵלָ֧ה וּטְרֵפָ֛ה לֹ֥א יֹאכַ֖ל לְטָמְאָה־בָ֑הּ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A carcass or [a] torn [animal] not he will eat, to become unclean by it; I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: A carcass or a torn [animal] he shall not eat, becoming unclean by it. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: He must not eat an animal that has died or one torn by wild beasts, and so become unclean by it. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: A priest must not eat an animal that died by itself or was killed by wild animals. It would make him unclean. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Animal muerto o [animal] despedazado no comerá, haciéndose impuro con ello. Yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: No comerá un animal que haya muerto ni uno despedazado por las fieras, para no quedar impuro por ello. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Un sacerdote no debe comer un animal que murió solo o que mataron las fieras. Eso lo haría impuro. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Une bête morte ou une [bête] déchirée, il ne la mangera pas, se rendant impur par elle. Je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Il ne mangera pas d’une bête morte ou d’une bête déchirée par les fauves, ce qui le rendrait impur. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Un prêtre ne doit pas manger un animal mort de lui-même ou tué par des bêtes sauvages. Cela le rendrait impur. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Mzoga au [mnyama] aliyeraruliwa hatakula, akawa najisi kwa sababu yake. Mimi [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Asile mnyama aliyekufa mwenyewe wala aliyeraruliwa na wanyama wakali, asije akawa najisi kwa sababu hiyo. Mimi ndimi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Kuhani asile mnyama aliyekufa mwenyewe au aliyeuawa na wanyama wa porini. Hilo lingemtia unajisi. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: a carcass or a torn animal: meat from an animal that was not slaughtered
decisions.reason: The blood of such an animal was not drained out (17:13-15). An ordinary Israelite who ate it became unclean until evening and had to wash (11:40; 17:15). For a priest it is forbidden outright, as Ezekiel 44:31 repeats.

decisions.choice: A priest
decisions.reason: Readable names who is meant, as in verse 6.

source.text: וְשָׁמְר֣וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֗י וְלֹֽא־יִשְׂא֤וּ עָלָיו֙ חֵ֔טְא וּמֵ֥תוּ ב֖וֹ כִּ֣י יְחַלְּלֻ֑הוּ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מְקַדְּשָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will keep my charge, and not they will bear on it sin and die by it, for they profane it; I [am] Yahweh [who] makes them holy.

en.L: And they shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} charge, and they shall not bear sin for it and die by it, because they profane it. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who makes them holy.
en.B: The priests must guard what I have entrusted to them, or they will bear sin because of the holy food and die for having profaned it. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who makes them holy.
en.R: The priests must obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} orders. If they do not, they will be guilty because of the holy food. They will die for treating it as if it were not holy. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who makes them holy.

es.L: Y guardarán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} encargo, y no cargarán con pecado por ello ni morirán por ello, porque lo habrán profanado. Yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} que los santifica.
es.B: Los sacerdotes guardarán lo que les he encomendado; de lo contrario, cargarán con pecado a causa de la comida santa y morirán por haberla profanado. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que los santifica.
es.R: Los sacerdotes tienen que obedecer {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} órdenes. Si no lo hacen, serán culpables a causa de la comida santa. Morirán por tratarla como si no fuera santa. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que los hace santos.

fr.L: Et ils garderont {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} charge, et ils ne porteront pas de péché à cause de cela et n’en mourront pas, parce qu’ils l’auraient profané. Je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui les sanctifie.
fr.B: Les prêtres garderont ce que je leur ai confié ; sinon, ils porteront un péché à cause de la nourriture sainte et mourront pour l’avoir profanée. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui les sanctifie.
fr.R: Les prêtres doivent obéir à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} ordres. Sinon, ils seront coupables à cause de la nourriture sainte. Ils mourront pour l’avoir traitée comme si elle n’était pas sainte. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui les rend saints.

sw.L: Nao watalinda agizo {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, wala hawatachukua dhambi kwa ajili yake na kufa kwa ajili yake, kwa sababu wamekitia unajisi. Mimi [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ninayewatakasa.
sw.B: Makuhani watalinda kile nilichowakabidhi; la sivyo watabeba dhambi kwa sababu ya chakula kitakatifu na kufa kwa kukitia unajisi. Mimi ndimi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ninayewatakasa.
sw.R: Lazima makuhani watii maagizo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Wasipotii, watakuwa na hatia kwa sababu ya chakula kitakatifu. Watakufa kwa kukitendea kana kwamba si kitakatifu. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ninayewafanya kuwa watakatifu.

decisions.choice: my charge: the duty I have given them to guard
decisions.reason: The word means something kept or guarded, and so an obligation. It is used of the priests' and Levites' duties at the sanctuary (8:35; Numbers 3:7-8; 18:3-5). Here it is the duty of keeping the holy food from being made common.

decisions.choice: for it ... by it ... profane it: the holy food
decisions.reason: "It" has no stated noun. It most likely means the holy food of verses 2-7, which the priest profanes by eating it while unclean. To bear sin is to carry its guilt and its penalty (19:17; 24:15).

decisions.choice: I am the LORD who makes them holy: God himself sets the priests apart
decisions.reason: The priests were made holy at their ordination (8:12, 30), but it is God who makes them holy (21:8, 15, 23). Because they belong to him, they must treat what is holy as his. See verse 32.

decisions.choice: The priests; the holy food
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "they" are and what "it" is, following m2.

decisions.choice: "que los santifica" (L, B); "que los hace santos" (R)
decisions.reason: "Santificar" is the established word for God making someone holy; Readable says the same in plain words. Kept for 22:16 and 22:32.

decisions.choice: "qui les sanctifie" (L, B); "qui les rend saints" (R)
decisions.reason: "Sanctifier" is the established word for God making someone holy; Readable says the same in plain words. The verb agrees with "le SEIGNEUR" ("Je suis le SEIGNEUR, qui les sanctifie"). Kept for 22:16 and 22:32.

decisions.choice: "ninayewatakasa" (L, B); "ninayewafanya kuwa watakatifu" (R)
decisions.reason: "Kutakasa" is the usual word for making holy; Readable spells it out as "make them holy". Kept for 22:16 and 22:32.

source.text: וְכָל־זָ֖ר לֹא־יֹ֣אכַל קֹ֑דֶשׁ תּוֹשַׁ֥ב כֹּהֵ֛ן וְשָׂכִ֖יר לֹא־יֹ֥אכַל קֹֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And any stranger not he will eat [a] holy thing; [a] settler of [a] priest and [a] hired worker not he will eat [a] holy thing.

en.L: And no stranger shall eat a holy thing; a settler of a priest or a hired worker shall not eat a holy thing.
en.B: No layperson may eat holy food. Neither a resident staying with a priest nor a worker he hires may eat it.
en.R: Only a priest's family may eat holy food. A person who lives with a priest or works for him for pay must not eat it.

es.L: Y ningún extraño comerá cosa santa; el residente de un sacerdote o el jornalero no comerá cosa santa.
es.B: Ningún laico podrá comer comida santa. Ni el que vive en casa de un sacerdote ni el trabajador que él contrata podrán comerla.
es.R: Solo la familia de un sacerdote puede comer la comida santa. Una persona que vive con un sacerdote o que trabaja para él por un sueldo no debe comerla.

fr.L: Et aucun profane ne mangera de chose sainte ; celui qui réside chez un prêtre ou le salarié ne mangera pas de chose sainte.
fr.B: Aucun laïc ne pourra manger de nourriture sainte. Ni celui qui habite chez un prêtre ni l’ouvrier qu’il engage ne pourront en manger.
fr.R: Seule la famille d’un prêtre peut manger la nourriture sainte. Quelqu’un qui vit chez un prêtre ou qui travaille pour lui contre un salaire ne doit pas en manger.

sw.L: Wala mtu wa nje yeyote hatakula kitu kitakatifu; mkaaji wa kuhani na mfanyakazi wa kuajiriwa hatakula kitu kitakatifu.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote asiye wa jamaa ya kuhani asile chakula kitakatifu. Mtu anayeishi kwa kuhani au mfanyakazi aliyemwajiri hawezi kukila.
sw.R: Ni jamaa ya kuhani tu wanaoweza kula chakula kitakatifu. Mtu anayeishi na kuhani au anayemfanyia kazi kwa ujira asile chakula hicho.

decisions.choice: stranger: anyone outside a priest's household, a layperson
decisions.reason: The word means one who is outside, an outsider to a particular group. Here it is anyone who does not belong to the household of a priest, even an Israelite (Numbers 3:10; 16:40; 18:4, 7). It is not the word for a sojourner (16:29) or for a foreigner (verse 25). Verses 10-13 then say who belongs to the household and who does not.

decisions.choice: a settler of a priest or a hired worker: people who live or work with a priest but are not his
decisions.reason: A settler is a resident without land of his own who lodges with others (25:6, 40), and a hired worker is paid by the day or the year (19:13). They may live in the priest's house, but they keep their freedom and are not part of his household. So they may not share its holy food.

decisions.choice: No layperson (Balanced); Only a priest's family (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Stranger" here does not mean a foreigner, so Balanced says "layperson" and Readable says who may eat. Literal keeps "stranger".

decisions.choice: "extraño" (L); "laico" (B)
decisions.reason: As in Numbers, "extraño" renders the outsider (zar), not the foreigner; Balanced says "laico", like the English "layperson", and keeps it in verses 12-13.

decisions.choice: "profane" (L); "laïc" (B)
decisions.reason: As in Numbers, "profane" renders the outsider (zar), anyone outside the priest's household, not a foreigner; Balanced says "laïc", like the English "layperson", and keeps it in verses 12-13.

decisions.choice: "mtu wa nje" (L); "mtu asiye wa jamaa ya kuhani" (B)
decisions.reason: "Mgeni" would mean a foreigner or sojourner. The outsider here is anyone outside a priest's household, so Literal says "mtu wa nje", as in Numbers, and Balanced says who is meant; Swahili has no common word for "layperson".

source.text: וְכֹהֵ֗ן כִּֽי־יִקְנֶ֥ה נֶ֨פֶשׁ֙ קִנְיַ֣ן כַּסְפּ֔וֹ ה֖וּא יֹ֣אכַל בּ֑וֹ וִילִ֣יד בֵּית֔וֹ הֵ֖ם יֹאכְל֥וּ בְלַחְמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [a] priest, when he buys [a] person, [the] purchase of his money, he will eat of it; and [the] born of his house, they will eat of his food.

en.L: But if a priest buys a person, the purchase of his money, he may eat of it; and those born in his house, they may eat of his food.
en.B: But a person whom a priest has bought with his money may eat of it, and so may the slaves born in his house. They may share his food.
en.R: But if a priest buys a slave, the slave may eat the holy food. So may slaves born in the priest's house. They may eat the priest's food.

es.L: Pero si un sacerdote compra una persona, adquisición de su dinero, esta podrá comer de ella; y los nacidos en su casa, ellos podrán comer de su alimento.
es.B: Pero la persona que un sacerdote haya comprado con su dinero podrá comer de ella, y también los esclavos nacidos en su casa. Ellos podrán compartir su comida.
es.R: Pero si un sacerdote compra un esclavo, ese esclavo puede comer la comida santa. También pueden comerla los esclavos nacidos en la casa del sacerdote. Pueden comer la comida del sacerdote.

fr.L: Mais un prêtre, s’il achète une personne, acquisition de son argent, celle-ci pourra en manger ; et ceux qui sont nés dans sa maison, eux pourront manger de sa nourriture.
fr.B: Mais la personne qu’un prêtre a achetée avec son argent pourra en manger, ainsi que les esclaves nés dans sa maison. Ils pourront partager sa nourriture.
fr.R: Mais si un prêtre achète un esclave, cet esclave peut manger la nourriture sainte. Les esclaves nés dans la maison du prêtre le peuvent aussi. Ils peuvent manger la nourriture du prêtre.

sw.L: Lakini kuhani akinunua mtu, mali iliyonunuliwa kwa fedha yake, huyo atakula katika hicho; na wale waliozaliwa nyumbani mwake, wao watakula katika chakula chake.
sw.B: Lakini mtu ambaye kuhani amemnunua kwa fedha yake anaweza kukila, na vilevile watumwa waliozaliwa nyumbani mwake. Wanaweza kushiriki chakula chake.
sw.R: Lakini kuhani akinunua mtumwa, mtumwa huyo anaweza kula chakula kitakatifu. Watumwa waliozaliwa nyumbani mwa kuhani wanaweza pia kukila. Wanaweza kula chakula cha kuhani.

decisions.choice: a person, bought with his money: a slave, who belongs to the priest's household
decisions.reason: A slave bought with money was part of the household, unlike the settler or the hired worker of verse 10. Such a slave was circumcised and ate the Passover with the family (Genesis 17:12-13; Exodus 12:44-45). So the slave may also eat the holy food. On slaves in Israel see 25:44-46.

decisions.choice: those born in his house: slaves born into the household
decisions.reason: The phrase means slaves born to slaves already in the house (Genesis 17:12; Jeremiah 2:14). They too belong to the household.

decisions.choice: slave(s)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "a person" and "those born in his house". Balanced says "slaves born in his house", and Readable says "slave" for both, following m1 and m2. "Slave" stays, as the style guide keeps it for people bought with money.

source.text: וּבַת־כֹּהֵ֔ן כִּ֥י תִהְיֶ֖ה לְאִ֣ישׁ זָ֑ר הִ֕וא בִּתְרוּמַ֥ת הַקֳּדָשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [a] daughter of [a] priest, when she becomes [the wife] of [a] man [who is a] stranger, she of [the] contribution of the holy things not she will eat.

en.L: And a daughter of a priest, if she belongs to a man [who is] a stranger, she shall not eat of the contribution of the holy things.
en.B: A priest's daughter who is married to a layman may not eat from the holy portions set aside as contributions.
en.R: If a priest's daughter marries a man who is not from a priest's family, she must not eat the holy food set apart for the priests.

es.L: Y la hija de un sacerdote, si es de un hombre extraño, no comerá de la ofrenda alzada de las cosas santas.
es.B: La hija de un sacerdote que esté casada con un laico no podrá comer de las porciones santas apartadas como contribuciones.
es.R: Si la hija de un sacerdote se casa con un hombre que no es de una familia de sacerdotes, no debe comer la comida santa apartada para los sacerdotes.

fr.L: Et la fille d’un prêtre, si elle est à un homme profane, ne mangera pas de l’offrande élevée des choses saintes.
fr.B: La fille d’un prêtre qui est mariée à un laïc ne pourra pas manger des portions saintes mises à part comme contributions.
fr.R: Si la fille d’un prêtre épouse un homme qui n’est pas d’une famille de prêtres, elle ne doit pas manger la nourriture sainte mise à part pour les prêtres.

sw.L: Na binti wa kuhani, akiwa wa mtu wa nje, yeye hatakula katika sadaka ya kuinuliwa ya vitu vitakatifu.
sw.B: Binti wa kuhani aliyeolewa na mtu asiye wa jamaa ya kuhani asile katika sehemu takatifu zilizotengwa kuwa michango.
sw.R: Binti wa kuhani akiolewa na mwanamume ambaye si wa jamaa ya makuhani, asile chakula kitakatifu kilichotengwa kwa ajili ya makuhani.

decisions.choice: belongs to a man who is a stranger: marries a man outside the priestly families
decisions.reason: "To be to a man" means to become his wife (Ruth 1:12-13). A married daughter becomes part of her husband's household. If he is not a priest, she no longer shares the holy food of her father's house.

decisions.choice: the contribution of the holy things: the holy portions set aside for the priests
decisions.reason: A contribution is what is lifted off and set aside from a larger whole for God and his priests, such as the thigh of the peace offering (7:32-34; 10:14-15) and the gifts listed in Numbers 18:11, 19. These were holy but not most holy, and the priest's daughters could eat them while they lived in his house (10:14).

decisions.choice: married to a layman / marries a man who is not from a priest's family
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "belongs to a man who is a stranger" means, following m1 and verse 10.

records.literal_gloss: And [a] daughter of [a] priest, when she becomes [a] widow or divorced, and offspring there is not to her, and she returns to [the] house of her father as [in] her youth, from [the] food of her father she will eat; and any stranger not he will eat of it.

en.L: But a daughter of a priest, if she becomes a widow or divorced and has no offspring, and returns to the house of her father as in her youth, she may eat of the food of her father; but no stranger shall eat of it.
en.B: But a priest's daughter who has lost her husband through death or divorce, who has no children, and who has returned to her father's house as when she was a girl, may again share her father's food. Still, no layperson may eat it.
en.R: But a priest's daughter may become a widow or be divorced. If she has no children and comes back to live in her father's house, as she did when she was young, she may eat her father's food. But no one outside a priest's family may eat it.

es.L: Pero la hija de un sacerdote, si queda viuda o repudiada, y no tiene descendencia, y vuelve a la casa de su padre como en su juventud, podrá comer del alimento de su padre; pero ningún extraño comerá de él.
es.B: Pero la hija de un sacerdote que haya perdido a su marido por muerte o por divorcio, que no tenga hijos y que haya vuelto a la casa de su padre como cuando era muchacha, podrá compartir otra vez la comida de su padre. Aun así, ningún laico podrá comerla.
es.R: Pero puede que la hija de un sacerdote quede viuda o se divorcie. Si no tiene hijos y vuelve a vivir en la casa de su padre, como cuando era joven, puede comer la comida de su padre. Pero nadie de fuera de la familia de un sacerdote debe comerla.

fr.L: Mais la fille d’un prêtre, si elle devient veuve ou répudiée, qu’elle n’a pas de descendance et qu’elle retourne à la maison de son père comme dans sa jeunesse, pourra manger de la nourriture de son père ; mais aucun profane n’en mangera.
fr.B: Mais la fille d’un prêtre qui a perdu son mari par la mort ou le divorce, qui n’a pas d’enfants et qui est revenue dans la maison de son père comme lorsqu’elle était jeune fille, pourra de nouveau partager la nourriture de son père. Toutefois, aucun laïc ne pourra en manger.
fr.R: Mais la fille d’un prêtre peut devenir veuve ou être divorcée. Si elle n’a pas d’enfants et revient vivre dans la maison de son père, comme quand elle était jeune, elle peut manger la nourriture de son père. Mais personne en dehors de la famille d’un prêtre ne doit en manger.

sw.L: Lakini binti wa kuhani akiwa mjane au aliyeachwa, naye hana uzao, akarudi nyumbani kwa baba yake kama katika ujana wake, atakula katika chakula cha baba yake; lakini mtu wa nje yeyote hatakula katika hicho.
sw.B: Lakini binti wa kuhani aliyefiwa na mumewe au aliyeachwa, asiye na watoto, naye amerudi nyumbani kwa baba yake kama alivyokuwa msichana, anaweza tena kushiriki chakula cha baba yake. Hata hivyo, mtu yeyote asiye wa jamaa ya kuhani asile chakula hicho.
sw.R: Lakini binti wa kuhani anaweza kuwa mjane au kuachwa na mumewe. Ikiwa hana watoto, naye amerudi kuishi nyumbani kwa baba yake kama alivyokuwa zamani akiwa msichana, anaweza kula chakula cha baba yake. Lakini mtu yeyote asiye wa jamaa ya kuhani asile chakula hicho.

decisions.choice: a widow or divorced, with no children, back in her father's house: she belongs to his household again
decisions.reason: With no husband and no children to support her, she returns to her father's house and is again counted in his household, as she was before her marriage. A widow or divorced woman who had children would belong with them. Tamar returned to her father's house in this way (Genesis 38:11).

decisions.choice: the food of her father: the holy food of verse 12
decisions.reason: Her father's food is the holy portions he receives as a priest (verse 7). She may share them again, but they remain closed to anyone outside the household (verse 10).

decisions.choice: who has lost her husband through death or divorce
decisions.reason: Balanced joins "widow or divorced" in one phrase. Literal and Readable keep the two words.

records.literal_gloss: And [a] man, when he eats [a] holy thing in error, and he will add its fifth to it and give to the priest the holy thing.

en.L: And if {{gender:anyone|a man}} eats a holy thing in error, then he shall add its fifth to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
en.B: If {{gender:anyone|any man}} eats holy food unintentionally, that person is to repay the priest for the holy food, adding a fifth to it.
en.R: {{gender:Someone|A man}} may eat holy food without meaning to. That person must pay the priest back for it and add one fifth more.

es.L: Y si {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} come una cosa santa por error, añadirá a ella su quinta parte y dará la cosa santa al sacerdote.
es.B: Si {{gender:alguien|algún hombre}} come comida santa sin intención, esa persona devolverá al sacerdote el valor de la comida santa, añadiendo una quinta parte.
es.R: {{gender:Alguien|Un hombre}} puede comer comida santa sin querer. Esa persona tiene que pagarle al sacerdote lo que comió y añadir una quinta parte más.

fr.L: Et si {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} mange une chose sainte par erreur, il y ajoutera un cinquième et donnera la chose sainte au prêtre.
fr.B: Si {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} mange de la nourriture sainte involontairement, cette personne remboursera au prêtre la valeur de la nourriture sainte, en y ajoutant un cinquième.
fr.R: {{gender:Quelqu’un|Un homme}} peut manger de la nourriture sainte sans le vouloir. Cette personne doit rembourser le prêtre et ajouter un cinquième en plus.

sw.L: Na mtu akila kitu kitakatifu kwa kukosea, ataongeza juu yake sehemu yake ya tano na kumpa kuhani kitu kitakatifu.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote akila chakula kitakatifu bila kukusudia, mtu huyo atamlipa kuhani thamani ya chakula hicho kitakatifu, akiongeza sehemu ya tano.
sw.R: Mtu anaweza kula chakula kitakatifu bila kukusudia. Lazima mtu huyo amlipe kuhani na kuongeza sehemu moja ya tano zaidi.

decisions.choice: add its fifth and give the holy thing: repay its value with a fifth more
decisions.reason: The person cannot give back food already eaten, so its value is given to the priest, with a fifth added, as for holy things used by mistake in 5:16. There a guilt offering is also brought.

decisions.choice: a man: anyone outside the priest's household
decisions.reason: The case follows verses 10-13: someone who may not eat holy food, man or woman, eats it without knowing. The word is "man", but the law covers anyone.

decisions.choice: anyone / a man
decisions.reason: The default is inclusive, following m2; the gender setting gives "a man" or "any man".

en.B: The priests must not profane the holy gifts that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set aside for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.R: The priests must not treat the holy gifts of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} as if they were not holy. These are the gifts the people set apart for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y no profanarán las cosas santas de los hijos de Israel, que ellos alzan para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}},
es.B: Los sacerdotes no profanarán las ofrendas santas que los israelitas apartan para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}},

fr.L: Et ils ne profaneront pas les choses saintes des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, qu’ils élèvent pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}},
fr.B: Les prêtres ne profaneront pas les dons saints que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} mettent à part pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}},
fr.R: Les prêtres ne doivent pas traiter les dons saints des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} comme s’ils n’étaient pas saints. Ce sont les dons que le peuple met à part pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Wala hawatavitia unajisi vitu vitakatifu vya wana wa Israeli, wanavyomwinulia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}},
sw.B: Makuhani wasiyatie unajisi matoleo matakatifu ambayo Waisraeli humtengea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}},
sw.R: Makuhani wasiyatendee matoleo matakatifu ya Waisraeli kana kwamba si matakatifu. Hayo ndiyo matoleo ambayo watu humtengea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: they shall not profane: the priests
decisions.reason: The subject is the priests, who are responsible for the holy gifts (verses 2 and 9). They profane them by letting someone who may not eat them do so (verse 16).

decisions.choice: lift up: set aside as a contribution
decisions.reason: The verb is the one from which "contribution" comes (verse 12): to lift off a part and give it to God.

decisions.choice: The priests
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, following m1.

en.L: and cause them to bear iniquity of guilt when they eat their holy things; for I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who makes them holy."
en.B: for if they let the people eat their holy gifts, they would load them with guilt that calls for a guilt offering. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who makes them holy."
en.R: They must not let other people eat those holy gifts. That would make the people guilty, and they would have to pay for it. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who makes them holy."

es.R: No deben dejar que otras personas coman esas ofrendas santas. Eso haría culpable a la gente, y tendrían que pagar por ello. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que los hace santos».

fr.L: ni ne leur feront porter la faute d’une culpabilité quand ils mangent leurs choses saintes ; car je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui les sanctifie. »
fr.B: car s’ils laissaient le peuple manger leurs dons saints, ils le chargeraient d’une culpabilité qui exige un sacrifice de réparation. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui les sanctifie. »
fr.R: Ils ne doivent pas laisser d’autres personnes manger ces dons saints. Cela rendrait ces gens coupables, et ils devraient payer pour cela. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui les rend saints. »

sw.L: wala hawatawatwika uovu wa hatia wanapokula vitu vyao vitakatifu; kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ninayewatakasa."
sw.B: kwa maana wakiwaacha watu wale matoleo yao matakatifu, watawatwika hatia inayodai sadaka ya hatia. Mimi ndimi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ninayewatakasa."
sw.R: Wasiwaache watu wengine wale matoleo hayo matakatifu. Hilo lingewafanya watu hao kuwa na hatia, nao wangelazimika kulipa. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ninayewafanya kuwa watakatifu."

decisions.choice: cause them to bear guilt when they eat: the priests bring guilt on lay Israelites by letting them eat
alternatives: they bring guilt on themselves when they eat
decisions.reason: "They" who cause are most likely the priests of verse 15, and "them" who bear the guilt and eat are the people, who eat what is holy without the right to it (verses 10, 14). The pronouns could also all refer to the priests: by eating the holy things while unclean they bring guilt on themselves.

decisions.choice: iniquity of guilt: guilt that must be paid for
decisions.reason: The second word is the one used for the guilt offering (5:15). The phrase describes guilt that requires reparation, as verse 14 and 5:16 set out.

decisions.choice: who makes them holy: the holy gifts, or the priests
decisions.reason: "Them" may be the holy gifts, which God makes holy, or the priests, as in verse 9. Either way God is the one who makes holy, and what he has made holy must not be treated as common.

decisions.choice: the people / other people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who eats, following m1.

records.literal_gloss: Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all [the] sons of Israel, and you will say to them, [a] man, [a] man of [the] house of Israel and of the sojourner in Israel who brings near his offering for all their vows and for all their freewill offerings which they bring near to Yahweh for [a] burnt offering,

en.L: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and say to them, '{{gender:Anyone|Any man}} of the house of Israel or of the sojourners in Israel who brings near his offering, for any of their vows or for any of their freewill offerings which they bring near to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a burnt offering,
en.B: "Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and tell them: '{{gender:Anyone|Any man}} from the people of Israel or from the outsiders living in Israel who presents an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a burnt offering, whether for a vow they have made or as a freewill offering,
en.R: "Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Tell them, 'Some of you may bring a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You may be from Israel or a stranger living in Israel. You may be keeping a promise you made to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, or you may just want to give a gift.

es.L: «Habla a Aarón y a sus hijos y a todos los hijos de Israel, y diles: “{{gender:Cualquiera|Cualquier hombre}} de la casa de Israel o de los inmigrantes en Israel que presente su ofrenda, por cualquiera de sus votos o por cualquiera de sus ofrendas voluntarias que presentan {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} como holocausto,

es.R: «Habla a Aarón, a sus hijos y a todos los israelitas. Diles: “Algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} traerán un holocausto {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Tal vez {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} de Israel o inmigrantes que viven en Israel. Tal vez {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} cumpliendo una promesa que le {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, o simplemente {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}} dar un regalo.

fr.L: « Parle à Aaron et à ses fils et à tous les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, et dis-leur : “{{gender:Quiconque|Tout homme}} de la maison d’Israël ou des immigrés en Israël qui fera approcher son offrande, pour l’un de leurs vœux ou pour l’une de leurs offrandes volontaires qu’ils font approcher {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} en holocauste,
fr.B: « Parle à Aaron, à ses fils et à tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, et dis-leur : “Lorsque {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} du peuple d’Israël ou des immigrés vivant en Israël présente {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} une offrande en holocauste, que ce soit pour un vœu qu’il a fait ou comme offrande volontaire,
fr.R: « Parle à Aaron, à ses fils et à tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Dis-leur : “Certains d’entre vous apporteront un holocauste {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Vous êtes peut-être d’Israël, ou des immigrés qui vivent en Israël. Vous tenez peut-être une promesse faite {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, ou vous voulez simplement faire un don.

sw.L: "Sema na Haruni na wanawe na wana wote wa Israeli, uwaambie, 'Mtu yeyote wa nyumba ya Israeli au wa wageni walio katika Israeli atakayesogeza sadaka yake, kwa ajili ya nadhiri zao zozote au kwa ajili ya sadaka zao zozote za hiari wanazomsogezea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa,

decisions.choice: Aaron, his sons and all Israel: rules for those who bring and those who receive
decisions.reason: The whole people is addressed, as in 17:2: the worshipers must bring sound animals, and the priests must refuse the others.

decisions.choice: a man, a man: anyone at all
decisions.reason: The doubled word means "anyone" (17:3, 8). The law is for every worshiper, man or woman, and it includes the outsiders who live among Israel (17:8).

decisions.choice: vows and freewill offerings: offerings promised to God, and offerings given freely
decisions.reason: A vow is an offering promised to God, often in return for help asked of him, and owed once the help comes (Genesis 28:20-22; 1 Samuel 1:11). A freewill offering is one given of one's own accord, without any promise or duty (7:16; Deuteronomy 12:6). Both could be burnt offerings or peace offerings (verse 21).

decisions.choice: Anyone / Any man
decisions.reason: The default is inclusive, following m2; the gender setting gives "any man". Readable speaks to the reader as "you".

decisions.choice: keeping a promise you made; just want to give a gift
decisions.reason: Readable says what a vow and a freewill offering are, following m3.

en.B: then, to be accepted for you, it must be a male without defect from the cattle, the sheep or the goats.
en.R: To be accepted, the animal must be a male with nothing wrong with it. It must be one of your cattle, sheep, or goats.

es.L: para {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} aceptación, [será] sin defecto, macho, del ganado vacuno, de las ovejas o de las cabras.
